ruling.explanation:
Addressed to both parties. The deviation is proven, but the way the driver explains it invokes an exculpatory clause against an artifact that is not in the bundle, and that forces a human review: no money moves, and the contested SGD 9.00 is held rather than collected or refunded.

The trip. The platform GPS trace (EV-GPS-02831) measures 29.13 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events; the booked optimal route (EV-TRIP-02831) is 21.9 km. The excess is 7.23 km, or 33.01% of optimal, so both POL-RD-01 tests pass (greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km absolute) and a route deviation is established. Under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs, not the rounded 29.1 km on the trip record. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 229 fixes at 10-second spacing, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0 s, so POL-RD-10(3) does not apply. Nothing else rescues or adds to the excess: the chat log (EV-CHAT-02831) is empty, so no rider-requested detour exists (POL-RD-04); no pickup or dropoff was amended (POL-RD-05); the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so the solo/pooled baseline is not in play (POL-RD-12); and no repeat-deviation pattern is established (deviation_flags_90d = 1 against 271 completed trips, below both POL-RD-06 thresholds), so no conduct referral fires. On the METERED fare (EV-FARE-02831), the POL-RD-02 arithmetic would be recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 21.9 + 0.28 x 29.6) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = SGD 29.3130 against a charged_total of SGD 37.07, a refund of 7.7570 rounded up to SGD 7.80, and nothing is added under POL-RD-09 because there are no ERP, toll or surcharge lines.

Why I cannot pay it. The driver explains the route by 'PIE was closed, LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-02831-01 covers it.' That advisory is present in the bundle only as a MISSING artifact - admissibility status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - so POL-RD-03 cannot be run against it and the excuse carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Critically, because the driver cited that missing identifier as his ground, POL-RD-13(1) expressly does not narrow POL-RD-10(5): an exculpatory clause (POL-RD-03) has been invoked against a cited artifact (EV-ADVIS-02831-01) that is missing from the pool. POL-RD-10(5) is a mandatory escalation trigger, and escalation under POL-RD-10 is terminal - it replaces the ruling, both money fields are null, and the disputed amount is held.

What would resolve it: a traffic_advisory covering this trip window that names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, carries a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached it, and states the shortest lawful alternative distance so the POL-RD-03 exoneration cap can be computed; or the driver withdrawing the closure assertion, in which case the deviation stands at 7.23 km and the POL-RD-02 partial refund of SGD 7.80 is the arithmetic result.

On the claims. The rider's claim that the driver 'cites no evidence ID for an advisory' misstates the record - the driver's statement names EV-ADVIS-02831-01 - and is rejected on that ground. The rider's further argument that the absent advisory cannot escalate was discarded by the referee with reason IMPAIRMENT_UNDISCLOSED and is not reinstated. Both sides' claims on the trace, the establishment tests, the fare arithmetic, the empty chat log, the absence of relocation or pooling, and the profile evidence are accepted; they do not change the outcome because the escalation is procedural. Every profile field mentioned (prior_deviation_flags, prior_no_show_flags and the rest) is context only under POL-GEN-01 and grounds nothing. Confidence is 0.70, the policy floor, because the escalation turns on a missing artifact that carries no weight of its own. No clause produces a referral, so the referrals list is empty.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
